claim: Plant nucleotide binding, leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors detect pathogen effectors and initiate an immune response.
source: Plant nucleotide binding, leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors detect pathogen effectors and initiate an immune response.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about NLR function in plant immunity.

claim: The structural basis of pathogen recognition by the integrated heavy metal associated (HMA) domain of the rice NLR Pikp was previously revealed.
source: Previously, we revealed the structural basis of pathogen recognition by the integrated heavy metal associated (HMA) domain of the rice NLR Pikp (Maqbool et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A mutation located within an effector-binding interface of the integrated Pikp–HMA domain increased the binding affinity for AVR-Pik variants in vitro and in vivo.
source: A mutation located within an effector-binding interface of the integrated Pikp–HMA domain increased the binding affinity for AVR-Pik variants in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including SPR, Y2H, and co-IP experiments.

claim: The mutation in Pikp-HMA translates to an expanded cell-death response to AVR-Pik variants previously unrecognized by Pikp in planta.
source: This translates to an expanded cell-death response to AVR-Pik variants previously unrecognized by Pikp in planta.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The structures of the engineered Pikp–HMA in complex with AVR-Pik variants revealed the mechanism of expanded recognition.
source: The structures of the engineered Pikp–HMA in complex with AVR-Pik variants revealed the mechanism of expanded recognition.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystal structure data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Protein engineering can improve the utility of plant NLR receptors where direct interaction between effectors and NLRs is established.
source: These results provide a proof-of-concept that protein engineering can improve the utility of plant NLR receptors where direct interaction between effectors and NLRs is established, particularly where this interaction occurs via integrated domains.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Plant NLRs are widely used in crop breeding programs because they confer resistance to disease.
source: Because they confer resistance to disease, plant NLRs are widely used in crop breeding programs (Dangl et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The recognition spectra of plant NLRs tend to be very specific.
source: However, the recognition spectra of plant NLRs tend to be very specific, and pathogens may delete detected effectors from their genome or evolve novel effector variants that are not detected by the NLRs to re-establish disease (Yoshida et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Pathogens may delete detected effectors from their genome or evolve novel effector variants that are not detected by NLRs to re-establish disease.
source: However, the recognition spectra of plant NLRs tend to be very specific, and pathogens may delete detected effectors from their genome or evolve novel effector variants that are not detected by the NLRs to re-establish disease (Yoshida et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Gain-of-function random mutagenesis has achieved some success in expanding the activation sensitivity or effector recognition profiles of NLRs.
source: Gain-of-function random mutagenesis has achieved some success in expanding the activation sensitivity or effector recognition profiles of NLRs (Segretin et al., 2014; Giannakopoulou et al., 2015; Harris et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NLRs can perceive protease effectors through their activity on engineered host proteins, which can lead to expanded recognition profiles.
source: An alternative strategy, in which NLRs perceive protease effectors through their activity on engineered host proteins, can lead to expanded recognition profiles (Carter et al., 2018; Helm et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Plant NLRs are modular proteins defined by their nucleotide-binding (NB-ARC) and leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domains.
source: Plant NLRs are modular proteins that are defined by their nucleotide-binding (NB-ARC) and leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domains, but that also have either an N-terminal coiled-coil (CC) or a Toll/Interleukin-1/Resistance-protein (TIR) signaling domain (Takken and Goverse, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and represents established knowledge.

claim: Many NLRs contain non-canonical integrated domains.
source: Many NLRs also contain non-canonical integrated domains (Kroj et al., 2016; Sarris et al., 2016; Bailey et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Integrated domains are thought to be derived from ancestral virulence-associated effector targets that directly bind pathogen effectors or are modified by them.
source: Integrated domains are thought to be derived from ancestral virulence-associated effector targets that directly bind pathogen effectors (or host proteins; Fujisaki et al., 2017) or are modified by them, thereby initiating an immune response (Cesari et al., 2014; Le Roux et al., 2015; Maqbool et al., 2015; Sarris et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NLRs containing integrated domains typically function in pairs, requiring a second genetically linked NLR for immune signaling.
source: NLRs containing integrated domains (often called the 'sensor') typically function in pairs, requiring a second genetically linked NLR (the 'helper') for immune signaling (Białas et al., 2018; Eitas and Dangl, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Two rice NLR pairs, Pik and Pia, contain an integrated Heavy Metal Associated (HMA) domain in their sensor NLR that directly binds effectors from the rice blast pathogen Magnaporthe oryzae.
source: Two rice NLR pairs, Pik and Pia, contain an integrated Heavy Metal Associated (HMA) domain in their sensor NLR that directly binds effectors from the rice blast pathogen Magnaporthe oryzae (also known as Pycularia oryzae) (Maqbool et al., 2015; Cesari et al., 2013; Ortiz et al., 2017; Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The integrated HMA domain in the sensor NLR Pik-1 directly binds the effector AVR-Pik.
source: The integrated HMA domain in the sensor NLR Pik-1 directly binds the effector AVR-Pik.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Co-evolutionary dynamics has driven the emergence of polymorphic Pik-1 HMA domains and AVR-Pik effectors in natural populations.
source: Co-evolutionary dynamics has driven the emergence of polymorphic Pik-1 HMA domains and AVR-Pik effectors in natural populations, and these display differential disease-resistance phenotypes (Costanzo and Jia, 2010; Kanzaki et al., 2012; Yoshida et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The Pikp NLR allele only responds to the effector variant AVR-PikD.
source: The Pikp NLR allele only responds to the effector variant AVR-PikD, but the Pikm allele responds to AVR-PikD, AVR-PikE, and AVR-PikA.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior work and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Pikm allele responds to AVR-PikD, AVR-PikE, and AVR-PikA.
source: The Pikp NLR allele only responds to the effector variant AVR-PikD, but the Pikm allele responds to AVR-PikD, AVR-PikE, and AVR-PikA.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior work and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The differential phenotypes of Pikp and Pikm can be recapitulated in the model plant Nicotiana benthamiana using a cell-death assay.
source: These phenotypes can be recapitulated in the model plant Nicotiana benthamiana using a cell-death assay, and are underpinned by differences in effector–receptor binding interfaces that lead to different affinities in vitro (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The differential phenotypes of Pikp and Pikm are underpinned by differences in effector–receptor binding interfaces that lead to different affinities in vitro.
source: These phenotypes can be recapitulated in the model plant Nicotiana benthamiana using a cell-death assay, and are underpinned by differences in effector–receptor binding interfaces that lead to different affinities in vitro (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A single-site mutation (Asn261Lys, Lys262Glu) in Pikp strengthens the cell-death response in N. benthamiana to AVR-PikD.
source: This single-site mutation strengthens the cell-death response in N. benthamiana to AVR-PikD, and gains a Pikm-like response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The Asn261Lys, Lys262Glu mutation in Pikp gains a Pikm-like response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA.
source: This single-site mutation strengthens the cell-death response in N. benthamiana to AVR-PikD, and gains a Pikm-like response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The gain-of-function phenotype of PikpNK-KE correlates with increased binding affinity of the effectors by the PikpNK-KE–HMA domain in vitro and in vivo.
source: We show that this gain-of-function phenotype correlates with increased binding affinity of the effectors by the PikpNK-KE–HMA domain in vitro and in vivo, and demonstrate that this mutation results in a Pikm-like structure for PikpNK-KE when in complex with AVR-Pik effectors.
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR, Y2H, and co-IP data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The Asn261Lys, Lys262Glu mutation results in a Pikm-like structure for PikpNK-KE when in complex with AVR-Pik effectors.
source: We show that this gain-of-function phenotype correlates with increased binding affinity of the effectors by the PikpNK-KE–HMA domain in vitro and in vivo, and demonstrate that this mutation results in a Pikm-like structure for PikpNK-KE when in complex with AVR-Pik effectors.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystal structure data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The newly engineered interface is responsible for the expanded response of PikpNK-KE.
source: Finally, we confirm that the newly engineered interface is responsible for the expanded response of PikpNK-KE by mutation of the effectors.
evidence: This claim is supported by effector mutation data presented in Figure 4.

claim: One double mutation in two adjacent amino-acid residues contained within interface 3, Asn261Lys and Lys262Glu (PikpNK-KE), induced cell death in response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA.
source: We found that one double mutation in two adjacent amino-acid residues contained within interface 3, Asn261Lys and Lys262Glu (henceforth PikpNK-KE), induced cell death in response to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 1.

claim: All of the Pikp mutant proteins were expressed in plants.
source: Western blots confirmed that all of the proteins were expressed in plants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: PikpNK-KE shows an effector hierarchy of AVR-PikD > AVR-PikE > AVR-PikA in cell death intensity.
source: When looking at the intensity of cell death mediated by PikpNK-KE, as for the Pikm allele (De la Concepcion et al., 2018), we observed an effector hierarchy of AVR-PikD > AVR-PikE > AVR-PikA .
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data presented in Figure 1.

claim: PikpNK-KE shows a comparable, but elevated response to effector variants when compared to that of Pikm.
source: PikpNK-KE shows a comparable, but elevated (not statistically significant in the case of AVR-PikE), response to effector variants when compared to that of Pikm (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 4.

claim: The cell-death response to AVR-PikD mediated by PikpNK-KE is similar but elevated when compared to that mediated by Pikp.
source: The cell-death response to AVR-PikD mediated by PikpNK-KE is similar but elevated when compared to that mediated by Pikp (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: PikpNK-KE does not show a response to the stealthy AVR-PikC variant.
source: PikpNK-KE does not show a response to the stealthy AVR-PikC variant.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The results of ion-leakage assays correlate well with the cell-death index scores based on autofluorescence.
source: The results of these assays correlate well with the cell-death index scores based on autofluorescence described above.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of data from Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: The single Asn261Lys/Lys262Glu (PikpNK-KE) mutation at interface 3 in the Pikp NLR expands this protein's recognition profile to include the effector variants AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, similar to that observed for Pikm.
source: We conclude that the single Asn261Lys/Lys262Glu (PikpNK-KE) mutation at interface 3 in the Pikp NLR expands this protein's recognition profile to include the effector variants AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA, similar to that observed for Pikm.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the cell death assay data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Increases in growth and in blue coloration were observed for Pikp-HMANK-KE with effectors AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA when compared with Pikp-HMA in Y2H assays.
source: Using Y2H, we observed increases in growth and in blue coloration (both indicative of protein–protein interaction) for Pikp-HMANK-KE with effectors AVR-PikE and, particularly, AVR-PikA when compared with Pikp-HMA (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Limited yeast growth was observed for Pikp-HMANK-KE with AVR-PikC at lower stringency in Y2H assays.
source: Unexpectedly, we also observed limited yeast growth for Pikp-HMANK-KE with AVR-PikC at the lower stringency (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Expression of all proteins was confirmed in yeast.
source: Expression of all proteins was confirmed in yeast (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Pikp-HMANK-KE mutant has a higher binding affinity for effectors AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA than does the wild-type protein as measured by SPR.
source: These data showed an increased binding of Pikp-HMANK-KE to AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA compared to that of wild-type Pikp (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The binding of Pikp-HMANK-KE to the AVR-Pik effectors was greater than that of Pikm-HMA as measured by SPR.
source: The binding of Pikp-HMANK-KE to the AVR-Pik effectors was also greater than that of Pikm-HMA (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 2), correlating with the results of cell-death assays (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Neither Pikp-HMA nor Pikm-HMA domains show binding to AVR-PikC by SPR.
source: Although neither Pikp-HMA nor Pikm-HMA domains show binding to AVR-PikC by SPR, we observe a gain-of-binding of this effector variant with Pikp-HMANK-KE (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: A gain-of-binding of AVR-PikC with Pikp-HMANK-KE was observed by SPR.
source: Although neither Pikp-HMA nor Pikm-HMA domains show binding to AVR-PikC by SPR, we observe a gain-of-binding of this effector variant with Pikp-HMANK-KE (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: The increased binding affinity of Pikp-HMANK-KE to effectors correlates with the expanded cell-death response in planta.
source: These results show that the Pikp-HMANK-KE mutant has a higher binding affinity for effectors AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA than does the wild-type protein. This suggests that the increased binding affinity to the HMA domain correlates with the expanded cell-death response in planta (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from comparing SPR data (Figure 2) with cell death data (Figure 1).

claim: AVR-PikD shows a robust association with Pikp-1 in co-IP experiments.
source: AVR-PikD shows a robust association with Pikp-1.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Association of AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA with the full-length Pikp-1 in planta was not detected by co-IP.
source: However, although we observe limited binding to the isolated Pikp-HMA domain in Y2H and SPR screens, we did not detect association of AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA with the full-length Pikp-1 in planta (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Clear association of AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA with the Pikp-1NK-KE mutant was observed by co-IP.
source: By contrast, we observe clear association of AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA with the Pikp-1NK-KE mutant, albeit with reduced intensity compared to AVR-PikD, correlating with the hierarchical cell-death response observed in planta (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A very low level of association between full-length Pikp-1NK-KE and AVR-PikC was detected by co-IP.
source: We also detect a very low level of association between full-length Pikp-1NK-KE and AVR-PikC (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Co-expression of Pikp-1NK-KE and AVR-PikC does not result in macroscopic cell death in N. benthamiana.
source: However, co-expression of Pikp-1NK-KE and AVR-PikC does not result in macroscopic cell death in N. benthamiana (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Effector variant association with full-length Pikp-1 and Pikp-1NK-KE correlates with the in planta cell-death response.
source: These results show that effector variant association with full-length Pikp-1 and Pikp-1NK-KE correlates with the in planta cell-death response (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from comparing co-IP data (Figure 2C) with cell death data (Figure 1C).

claim: The crystal structures of Pikp-HMANK-KE bound to AVR-PikD and to AVR-PikE were determined.
source: To this end, we determined the crystal structures of Pikp-HMANK-KE bound to AVR-PikD, and to AVR-PikE.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure data presented in the manuscript.

claim: X-ray diffraction data for Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikD were collected to 1.6 Å resolution.
source: Each complex was crystallized (see Materials and methods) and X-ray diffraction data were collected at the Diamond Light Source (Oxford, UK) to 1.6 Å and 1.85 Å resolution, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: X-ray diffraction data for Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikE were collected to 1.85 Å resolution.
source: Each complex was crystallized (see Materials and methods) and X-ray diffraction data were collected at the Diamond Light Source (Oxford, UK) to 1.6 Å and 1.85 Å resolution, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: The overall architecture of Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-Pik complexes is the same as that observed for all Pik-HMA/AVR-Pik effector structures.
source: The overall architecture of these complexes is the same as that observed for all Pik-HMA/AVR-Pik effector structures.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of the new structures with previously determined structures.

claim: A key interaction at interface 3 involves a lysine residue (Lys262 in Pikp and Pikm) that forms intimate contacts within a pocket on the effector surface.
source: A key interaction at interface 3, one of the previously defined Pik-HMA–AVR-Pik interfaces (De la Concepcion et al., 2018), involves a lysine residue (Lys262 in Pikp and Pikm) that forms intimate contacts within a pocket on the effector surface (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In Pikp, regions adjacent to Lys262 have to loop-out to position this lysine in the effector pocket, compromising the packing at the interface.
source: In order to position this lysine in the effector pocket, Pikp has to loop-out regions adjacent to this residue, compromising the packing at the interface (De la Concepcion et al., 2018, Figure 3A [left panel], B [left panel], C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3 and cited prior work.

claim: In Pikm, no looping-out is required to locate the lysine within the effector pocket because the position of the lysine is shifted one residue to the N-terminus.
source: By contrast, in Pikm, where the position of the lysine is shifted one residue to the N-terminus, no looping-out is required to locate the lysine within the pocket (Figure 3A [right panel], B [right panel], C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In the PikpNK-KE mutant, the position of the key lysine is shifted one residue to the N-terminus compared to that in the wild-type, so that it occupies the same position in the PikpNK-KE sequence as in the Pikm sequence.
source: In the PikpNK-KE mutant, the position of this key lysine is shifted one residue to the N-terminus compared to that in the wild-type, so that it occupies the same position in the PikpNK-KE sequence as in the Pikm sequence.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence analysis and structural data.

claim: In the crystal structures of Pikp-HMANK-KE in complex with either AVR-PikD or AVR-PikE, the interface region adopts a Pikm-like conformation with no looping-out of the preceding structure.
source: In the crystal structures of Pikp-HMANK-KE in complex with either AVR-PikD or AVR-PikE, we see that this region of the HMA adopts a Pikm-like conformation (Figure 3A [middle panel], B [middle panel], C and D), with no looping-out of the preceding structure.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3.

claim: By making the PikpNK-KE mutant, Pikp was resurfaced to have a more robust, Pikm-like interface in the interface 3 region.
source: This confirms that in making the PikpNK-KE mutant, we have resurfaced Pikp to have a more robust, Pikm-like interface in this region.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the structural data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Only limited structural perturbations at interface 1 or 2 resulted from the binding of the AVR-PikD or AVR-PikE effectors to Pikp-HMA or Pikp-HMANK-KE.
source: We found only limited structural perturbations at either of the other previously defined interfaces (interface 1 or 2 [De la Concepcion et al., 2018]) resulting from the binding of the AVR-PikD or AVR-PikE effectors to Pikp-HMA or Pikp-HMANK-KE (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The effects of the PikpNK-KE mutant on protein function are mediated by altered interactions at interface 3.
source: We therefore conclude that the effects of the PikpNK-KE mutant on protein function are mediated by altered interactions at interface 3.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the structural data.

claim: Cell death in N. benthamiana is essentially blocked when co-expressing either Pikp or PikpNK-KE with the AVR-PikDH46E mutant.
source: We found that cell death in N. benthamiana is essentially blocked when co-expressing either Pikp or PikpNK-KE with this mutant (AVR-PikDH46E), suggesting that the engineered NLR is still reliant on this interface for response (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The AVR-PikDH46E mutant displays some interaction with Pikp-HMANK-KE in Y2H assays.
source: Intriguingly, Y2H shows that the AVR-PikDH46E mutant displays some interaction with Pikp-HMANK-KE (Figure 4B), similar to this mutant's interaction with Pikm-HMA (De la Concepcion et al., 2018), although this interaction is barely observed by co-IP with the full-length NLR (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The interaction between AVR-PikDH46E and Pikp-HMANK-KE is barely observed by co-IP with the full-length NLR.
source: Intriguingly, Y2H shows that the AVR-PikDH46E mutant displays some interaction with Pikp-HMANK-KE (Figure 4B), similar to this mutant's interaction with Pikm-HMA (De la Concepcion et al., 2018), although this interaction is barely observed by co-IP with the full-length NLR (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The AVR-PikDE53R mutant has essentially no effect on recognition of the effector by PikpNK-KE in N. benthamiana.
source: We found that the AVR-PikDE53R mutant has essentially no effect on recognition of the effector by PikpNK-KE in N. benthamiana, and little or no effect on the interaction with Pikp-HMANK-KE or full-length PikpNK-KE (Figure 4A,B,C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death, Y2H, and co-IP data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The E53R mutation in AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA restricted the cell-death response in N. benthamiana.
source: By contrast, the equivalent mutation in AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA restricted the cell-death response in N. benthamiana, reduced the binding to Pikp-HMANK-KE in Y2H (as shown by the reduced blue coloration) and produced a less intense band for the effector following PikpNK-KE co-IP (Figure 4A,B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The E53R mutation in AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA reduced the binding to Pikp-HMANK-KE in Y2H.
source: By contrast, the equivalent mutation in AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA restricted the cell-death response in N. benthamiana, reduced the binding to Pikp-HMANK-KE in Y2H (as shown by the reduced blue coloration) and produced a less intense band for the effector following PikpNK-KE co-IP (Figure 4A,B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Y2H data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The E53R mutation in AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA produced a less intense band for the effector following PikpNK-KE co-IP.
source: By contrast, the equivalent mutation in AVR-PikE and AVR-PikA restricted the cell-death response in N. benthamiana, reduced the binding to Pikp-HMANK-KE in Y2H (as shown by the reduced blue coloration) and produced a less intense band for the effector following PikpNK-KE co-IP (Figure 4A,B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The expression of all proteins in yeast was confirmed by western blot.
source: The expression of all proteins in yeast was confirmed by western blot (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Interactions across interface 2 remain important for the PikpNK-KE interaction with AVR-Pik effectors.
source: These results provide evidence to show that while interactions across interface 2 remain important for the PikpNK-KE interaction with AVR-Pik effectors, it is the altered interaction at interface 3, as observed in the structures, that is responsible for the expanded recognition profile of this engineered mutant.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the effector mutation data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The altered interaction at interface 3 is responsible for the expanded recognition profile of the PikpNK-KE engineered mutant.
source: These results provide evidence to show that while interactions across interface 2 remain important for the PikpNK-KE interaction with AVR-Pik effectors, it is the altered interaction at interface 3, as observed in the structures, that is responsible for the expanded recognition profile of this engineered mutant.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the effector mutation data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Engineered plant NLR-type intracellular immune receptors have the potential to improve disease-resistance breeding.
source: Although largely elusive to date, engineered plant NLR-type intracellular immune receptors have the potential to improve disease-resistance breeding (Dangl et al., 2013; Rodriguez-Moreno et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and represents a speculative statement about future potential.

claim: NLR-integrated domains are a particularly attractive target for protein engineering because they interact directly with pathogen effectors.
source: NLR-integrated domains are a particularly attractive target for protein engineering because they interact directly with pathogen effectors (or host effector targets).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from established knowledge about integrated domains.

claim: Where tested, the binding affinities of integrated domains in vitro correlate with in planta immunity phenotypes.
source: Further, where tested, their binding affinities in vitro correlate with in planta immunity phenotypes (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2018), allowing biochemical and structural techniques to inform NLR design directly.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The recognition profile of the rice NLR Pikp can be expanded to include different AVR-Pik variants by engineering the binding interface between these proteins.
source: Here, we show that the recognition profile of the rice NLR Pikp can be expanded to include different AVR-Pik variants by engineering the binding interface between these proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Tighter binding affinity between effectors and integrated HMA domains correlates with increased immune signaling in plants.
source: This strengthens the hypothesis that tighter binding affinity between effectors and integrated HMA domains correlates with increased immune signaling in plants.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript and prior work.

claim: Tighter binding affinity between effectors and integrated HMA domains correlating with increased immune signaling was previously shown for both natural alleles of Pik and for Pia.
source: This was previously shown for both natural alleles of Pik (Maqbool et al., 2015; De la Concepcion et al., 2018) and for Pia (Guo et al., 2018), but is now also shown for an engineered NLR.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The correlation between tighter binding affinity and increased immune signaling may be a general model for integrated domains that directly bind effectors.
source: We propose this may be a general model for integrated domains that directly bind effectors.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the data.

claim: Natural variation in Pik NLRs has given rise to different effector recognition profiles.
source: Natural variation in Pik NLRs has given rise to different effector recognition profiles, and contributions from different binding interfaces were suggested to underpin this phenotype (De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A more favorable interaction at interface 3 in Pikm, compared to that in Pikp, was concluded to have evolved to compensate for changes in binding at interface 2.
source: In particular, a more favorable interaction at one interface (interface 3) in Pikm, compared to that in Pikp, was concluded to have evolved to compensate for changes in binding at a different site (interface 2).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from prior work.

claim: By mutating residues in Pikp (forming PikpNK-KE), favorable interfaces from Pikp and Pikm were combined into a single protein.
source: Here, through mutation of residues in Pikp (forming PikpNK-KE), we have combined favorable interfaces from Pikp and Pikm into a single protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Combining favorable interfaces from Pikp and Pikm resulted in an expanded recognition phenotype for effector binding and response in planta.
source: This has resulted in an expanded recognition phenotype for effector binding and response in planta.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In vitro, the binding of PikpNK-KE-HMA to effector variants is consistently higher than that of Pikm-HMA.
source: In vitro, the binding of PikpNK-KE-HMA to effector variants is consistently higher than that of Pikm-HMA (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The higher binding of PikpNK-KE-HMA to effector variants is likely underpinned by differences in a cluster of key residues within interface 2 that form more energetically favorable contacts.
source: This is likely to be underpinned by differences in a cluster of key residues within interface 2 (spatially equivalent residues Val222, Lys228, and Glu230 in Pikp, and Ala223, Gln229, and Val231 in Pikm) that form more energetically favorable contacts, including water-mediated hydrogen bonds.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: Despite a positive trend in binding, the levels of cell death mediated by Pikm and PikpNK-KE in planta are comparable.
source: However, despite a positive trend (which is significant in some cases), the levels of cell death mediated by Pikm and PikpNK-KE in planta are comparable (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 4.

claim: The PikpNK-KE mutant did not deliver a cell-death response in N. benthamiana to the stealthy AVR-PikC effector variant.
source: Although the PikpNK-KE mutant did not deliver a cell-death response in N. benthamiana to the stealthy AVR-PikC effector variant, it did show a gain-of-binding in vitro, as well as weak binding in Y2H and in in planta co-IP.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell death assay data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The PikpNK-KE mutant showed a gain-of-binding to AVR-PikC in vitro, as well as weak binding in Y2H and in in planta co-IP.
source: Although the PikpNK-KE mutant did not deliver a cell-death response in N. benthamiana to the stealthy AVR-PikC effector variant, it did show a gain-of-binding in vitro, as well as weak binding in Y2H and in in planta co-IP.
evidence: This claim is supported by SPR, Y2H, and co-IP data presented in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: The gain-of-binding for AVR-PikC observed in vitro is not sufficiently robust for binding or for triggering immune signaling in the context of the full-length NLR.
source: It is surprising that the gain-of-binding for AVR-PikC in vitro, unlike that for AVR-PikA, does not correlate directly with gain of in vivo interactions or cell-death response in N. benthamiana. We hypothesize that this gain-of-binding for AVR-PikC observed in vitro is not sufficiently robust, especially in the context of the full-length NLR, for binding or for triggering immune signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the data.

claim: Future interface engineering experiments may further improve the response profiles of Pik NLRs to currently unrecognized effector variants.
source: Nevertheless, this work sets the scene for future interface engineering experiments that may further improve the response profiles of Pik NLRs to currently unrecognized effector variants.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future work.

claim: Future work should test the disease resistance profile of M. oryzae strains carrying the different effector variants in rice expressing the engineered receptor.
source: It also suggests that future work should test the disease resistance profile of M. oryzae strains carrying the different effector variants in rice expressing the engineered receptor.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future work.

claim: The integrated HMA domain in the NLR RGA5 binds to M. oryzae effectors AVR1-CO39 and AVR-Pia via a different interface.
source: The integrated HMA domain in the NLR RGA5 (the sensor of the Pia NLR pair in rice) binds to M. oryzae effectors AVR1-CO39 and AVR-Pia via a different interface, and it has been suggested that these binding sites are mutually exclusive (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: It has been suggested that the binding sites for AVR1-CO39 and AVR-Pia on RGA5-HMA are mutually exclusive.
source: The integrated HMA domain in the NLR RGA5 (the sensor of the Pia NLR pair in rice) binds to M. oryzae effectors AVR1-CO39 and AVR-Pia via a different interface, and it has been suggested that these binding sites are mutually exclusive (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: An HMA domain could potentially be engineered to bind and respond to multiple effectors.
source: This raises the possibility that an HMA domain could be engineered to bind and respond to multiple effectors (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from prior work.

claim: The Pikp-HMA domain was shown to interact with AVR-Pia at the same interface as that used by the RGA5-HMA domain.
source: Recently, the Pikp-HMA domain was shown to interact with AVR-Pia at the same interface as that used by the RGA5-HMA domain, and this probably underpins the partial resistance of rice plants to M. oryzae expressing AVR-Pia (Varden et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The interaction between Pikp-HMA and AVR-Pia probably underpins the partial resistance of rice plants to M. oryzae expressing AVR-Pia.
source: Recently, the Pikp-HMA domain was shown to interact with AVR-Pia at the same interface as that used by the RGA5-HMA domain, and this probably underpins the partial resistance of rice plants to M. oryzae expressing AVR-Pia (Varden et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The interaction between Pikp-HMA and AVR-Pia presents a starting point for using Pikp as a chassis for engineering studies.
source: This presents a starting point for the use of Pikp as a chassis for such studies.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from prior work.

claim: It remains to be seen whether any resurfaced HMA domain can bind to multiple effectors.
source: Although it remains to be seen whether any such resurfaced HMA domain can bind to multiple effectors, these studies suggest that this strategy has potential as a novel approach.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future possibilities.

claim: Plant breeding is required to provide new genetic solutions to disease resistance in crops.
source: Plant breeding is required to provide new genetic solutions to disease resistance in crops.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge and inference.

claim: New genetic solutions to disease resistance are necessary to limit the environmental and social damage caused by pesticides.
source: This is necessary to limit the environmental and social damage caused by pesticides, and to deal with changes in climate and in the globalization of agriculture that result in the spread of pathogens and pests into new environments (Islam et al., 2016; Michelmore et al., 2017; Savary et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Classical breeding for disease resistance has been limited by issues such as linkage drag and hybrid incompatibility.
source: Classical breeding for disease resistance has been limited by issues such as linkage drag and hybrid incompatibility, as also seen in model plant species (Bomblies et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Novel molecular approaches such as engineering 'decoys' and protein resurfacing offer the opportunity for more targeted approaches to breeding for disease resistance.
source: Novel molecular approaches such as engineering 'decoys' (Kim et al., 2016) and protein resurfacing, as described here, combined with modern transformation (Altpeter et al., 2016) and breeding pipelines (Watson et al., 2018), offer the opportunity for more targeted approaches to breeding for disease resistance.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the current work and prior work.

claim: Protein resurfacing strategies will complement other emerging technologies in NLR identification and NLR stacking as methods to develop improved crops for the future.
source: These strategies will complement other emerging technologies in NLR identification (Arora et al., 2019) and NLR stacking (Dangl et al., 2013) as methods to develop improved crops for the future.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future applications.

claim: Protein structures and the data used to derive them have been deposited at the Protein DataBank (PDB) with accession codes 6R8K (Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikD) and 6R8M (Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikE).
source: Protein structures, and the data used to derive them, have been deposited at the Protein DataBank (PDB) with accession codes 6R8K (Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikD) and 6R8M (Pikp-HMANK-KE/AVR-PikE).
evidence: This is a statement of data deposition.
